title: Moving to the Astoria and the Sunday jitney dance
summary: Humphrey describes the Astoria job, pay of about $78, and the suburban jitney dance at La Vida.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: I didn't wake there for two years. And then, we got to the poppy, you know, and come and sign us at the Astor, you know? Rene was waking at the Astor until, you know, Sunday night until 12 o'clock. Then, we take over at 12.30, you know, after our dance, make $78. Mm-hmm. Got poppy there, and he had a place out there in Sue's Bay. Oh, Ridley was waking up there. Ridley and Schatz, Libby Ridley. Libby was playing drum, yes.
Was it near Jack Sheen's place? Yeah, at that Sue's Bay. Yeah, was it near Jack Sheen's up around there? Yeah.
Near the suburban gardens, right there? Yeah, on the other side of the suburban gardens. Right there, huh?

Yeah. They had a colored place out there. Mm-hmm. When out there, you know, after all this, after you finish on the out, first we let that jitney dance, for, you know, about a month, you know, every Sunday night, just a crowd, yeah, I think. Yeah.
What was the name of the jitney plays?
La Vida. La La Vida, huh?

Oh man, they, they had, they'd use a hundred, hundred birds, you know, they had all the time. Weekdays and on weekends, man, $150. Well, they spend your money, man, you get a dollar worth of tickets for ten cents a dance, man, and four dancers, you got them, and then take them tickets away from you. Mm-hmm. Well, that's kind of skin game.
